## 1. Figma Motion to Lottie: A Small-Business Motion System That Won’t Kill Core Web Vitals
- Target keyword: Figma Motion Lottie website | Secondary: Lottie export Figma marketing site, website micro-animation design system
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: how-to
- Angle: Teach DIY redesigners and aspiring designers how to use Figma Motion’s new reusable custom animation styles + Lottie/dotLottie export for marketing-site micro-interactions — while budgeting duration, file weight, and reduced-motion — so motion supports clarity instead of tanking LCP/INP. Complements the live CWV overview without repeating the INP triage playbook.
- Why now: Figma announced Motion custom styles, audio, text animations, and Lottie/dotLottie export on 2026-09-30 (open beta), with Plugin API support the same day — https://forum.figma.com/product-updates-3/motion-adds-custom-styles-audio-text-animations-and-lottie-export-58554 · https://developers.figma.com/docs/plugins/updates/2026/09/30/version-1-update-140/
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: What Motion just made reusable (styles, text, Lottie export)
  - H2: Which SMB site moments deserve motion (and which don’t)
  - H2: Build a 5-style motion sticker sheet before you animate pages
  - H2: Export checklist: Lottie vs video vs CSS for heroes and UI
  - H2: Performance + accessibility gates (weight, autoplay, prefers-reduced-motion)
  - H2: When motion craft means you need a designer/dev pass

## 2. Webflow Agent Instructions from Your Live Site vs Hiring a Designer: What Auto-Drafted Guidelines Still Miss
- Target keyword: Webflow Agent Instructions vs hiring designer | Secondary: Webflow generate design system guidelines, AI brand guidelines from website
- Search intent: Commercial investigation
- Format: comparison
- Angle: Map Webflow’s Agent Instructions Generation (Brand / Design System / Asset / CMS guidelines drafted from the live site) against what a human designer still owns — offer clarity, conversion IA, accessibility policy, and “what not to generate” — so SMB owners don’t treat auto-drafted agent rules as a finished design system. Distinct from live Webflow MCP agents post and from prior DESIGN.md / context-engineering ideas (this is site→agent instructions, not a blank brief).
- Why now: Webflow launched Agent Instructions Generation on 2026-09-02 so agents draft Brand, Design System, Asset, and CMS guidelines straight from the actual site instead of a blank editor — https://webflow.com/updates/agent-instructions-generation
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: What Agent Instructions Generation drafts from your site
  - H2: What the auto-draft usually gets right (tokens, components, CMS shape)
  - H2: What still needs a human (positioning, proof, WCAG, conversion rules)
  - H2: Side-by-side: DIY agent guidelines vs studio-owned design system
  - H2: Hybrid path: generate → designer edit → lock before agents ship pages
  - H2: Questions to ask any designer about agent-ready guidelines

## 4. Gutenberg 24.1 Design Tools: When Text Shadow and New Block Styles Help (or Hurt) a Small Business Site
- Target keyword: Gutenberg text shadow WordPress design | Secondary: Gutenberg 24.1 design tools small business, WordPress block design consistency
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: trend-opinion
- Angle: Use Gutenberg 24.1’s design-tool consistency wave (~140 PRs) and expanded text-shadow support (theme.json + Global Styles + Paragraph/Heading) to coach DIY WordPress owners: when decorative type helps hierarchy, when it fails contrast/readability, and when inconsistent block styling means you need a designer to set Global Styles once instead of decorating page-by-page.
- Why now: WordPress published “What’s new in Gutenberg 24.1?” on 2026-09-30, highlighting design-tool parity across core blocks and full text-shadow support in theme.json and Global Styles — https://make.wordpress.org/core/2026/09/30/whats-new-in-gutenberg-24-1-30-september/
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Low–Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: What Gutenberg 24.1 actually changed for non-developers
  - H2: Text shadow: good hierarchy vs bad contrast (WCAG-minded rules of thumb)
  - H2: Set Global Styles once — stop restyling every block
  - H2: A DIY “before you ship” visual QA for service pages
  - H2: Where aspiring designers add value (type system, restraint, a11y)
  - H2: Signs you’ve outgrown solo block decorating

## 5. Webflow CMS Components in Rich Text: A Conversion Design Playbook for Blog and Service Pages
- Target keyword: Webflow CMS components rich text | Secondary: Webflow CTA components in blog posts, Webflow conversion components CMS
- Search intent: Informational
- Format: playbook
- Angle: Show DIY Webflow owners how to drop reusable CTA, testimonial, and pricing components into CMS rich text (canvas or CMS panel) so blog/service content converts — with guardrails from Webflow’s own limits (no Collection Lists inside, no CMS-bound props/slots) — and when a studio should design the component system first. Distinct from MCP-agents and Agent Instructions ideas.
- Why now: Webflow launched “Add components to CMS content” on 2026-09-02 so any component can sit in rich text with per-instance properties, aimed at conversion-oriented CMS content — https://webflow.com/updates/add-components-to-cms-content
- Volume / KD: unverified
- Effort: Low–Medium
- Outline starter:
  - H2: What you can (and can’t) drop into CMS rich text
  - H2: Build a small conversion component kit (CTA, proof, pricing, FAQ tease)
  - H2: Editorial workflow: draft → insert → property pass → publish
  - H2: Responsive QA with side-by-side breakpoints before you ship
  - H2: Common DIY mistakes (too many CTAs, unstyled embeds, orphan components)
  - H2: When the component system needs a designer before more blog posts
